_authority: Owner, 2026-10-15 (L49 step 3, 2.27.0): 'the factory proposes, per sub-topic, how theory can be taught as activity, and the operator ticks or strikes each on the Stage 2 page.' And: 'if some theory easily can be taught as test, interactive, practical activity, active learning theory, be my guest - but first it needs to be reviewed by the person who uses the plugin, mostly a person who knows nothing in IT and almost everything in maritime.' The catalogue Claude proposes from; the proposals are written into architecture.json (modules[].active_learning) and decided on the Stage 2 page. How to write them: active/GUIDE.md. Read by scripts/make_architecture_page.py and scripts/active_plan.py.
rules: At least one proposal per programme sub-topic that carries theory - or a line saying why it stays plain ("technique": "plain", with "why").
The theory is never removed. A proposal takes MINUTES from plain theory, not slides: the slides stay, the instructor moves through them faster, their words stay to be read.
Written for a maritime expert who knows nothing about IT: what the trainees DO, in one or two plain sentences, in the operator's language. No technique names, no file or tool names.
Each proposal names its minutes, and what it needs that the factory cannot make alone (a photo of the real panel, the simulator, a piece of equipment) - in "needs".
Nothing is built from a proposal until the operator keeps it. A struck proposal stays in the file, marked struck, and is never proposed again for that sub-topic unless the operator asks.
The programme's hours do not change (L1). Practical hours are already active; proposals are for theory hours.

predict-then-reveal.fits: a process, a cause and its effect, a physical property - what happens when something changes
predict-then-reveal.does: The trainees predict what happens, on the tablet or aloud; then the slide or animation shows it, and they compare.
predict-then-reveal.example: Before the slide on boil-off: 'The tank is cooled to -162 °C and the ship sails into the tropics. What happens to the pressure, and why?' - then the process animation runs.

explain-then-reveal.fits: a principle or a reason - why a rule exists, why a design is as it is
explain-then-reveal.does: In pairs the trainees explain the reason to each other first; then the slide reveals it and they check what they missed.
explain-then-reveal.example: 'Why does a type C tank need no secondary barrier?' - two minutes in pairs, then the slide.

worked-example.fits: a calculation, a reading, a procedure with numbers - cargo quantity, a gas reading, a trim and stability figure
worked-example.does: The instructor works one example on the screen step by step; the trainees do the next one themselves on the tablet, then the next with fewer hints.
worked-example.example: One cargo quantity calculation worked on the screen; the trainees do the second with the same table.

scenario.fits: a decision, an emergency, a procedure under changing conditions - what the officer does
scenario.does: A real situation unfolds step by step; at each step the trainees decide what to do and why, and see what follows.
scenario.example: Gas alarm in the compressor room during loading: what first, who is told, what is closed - three decisions, each with its consequence.

explore.fits: equipment, a structure, a system - what has a shape, an inside or a layout in space
explore.does: The trainees turn, open and search the 3D model or interactive drawing themselves, and find the parts the instructor names.
explore.example: The four tank types in a hull section: each trainee opens them and finds which one leans on the hull for its strength.

self-check.fits: a block of theory just taught - a quick check that it landed
self-check.does: A few questions on the trainee tablet - operate, sort, tap, decide - with the trainee's own score at the end.
self-check.example: After the tank types: sort six photographs into the four types; tap the secondary barrier on the drawing.

statuses._old: An entry with no status was written before 2.27.0 and counts as kept.
